en: Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena, Section 6:
The Question on the Factors of Enlightenment (Bojjhaṅga)
“How many, venerable Nāgasena, are the factors of enlightenment?
“There are seven, great king, that are the factors of enlightenment.”
“But by how many factors of enlightenment, venerable sir, does one awaken?
“By one factor of enlightenment, great king, does one awaken: by the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment.
“Then why, venerable sir, are they called the ‘seven factors of enlightenment’?”
“What do you think, great king? If a sword were placed in its scabbard and not grasped by the hand, would it be able to cut what needs to be cut?
“In the same way, great king, without the factor of enlightenment that is the investigation of phenomena, one does not awaken by means of the [other] six factors of enlightenment.”
This concludes the sixth problem, on the factors of enlightenment.
